title: Mexican Economy Grows 3.2% Annually in the Third Quarter of 2026, Its Biggest Advance in Three Years
author: El Chamuco Staff
content:
_This article by El Chamuco Staff originally appeared in the[October 30, 2026
edition of El Chamuco](https://elchamuco.com.mx/2026/10/30/economia-mexicana-
crece-3-2-anual-en-el-tercer-trimestre-de-2026-su-mayor-avance-en-tres-anos/),
a Mexican political satire and news magazine._

_(October 30, 2026).— GDP rose 0.9% compared with the previous quarter, driven
by services and industry, while agricultural activities registered a
contraction. The result corresponds to INEGI 's timely estimate._

The Mexican economy registered **annual growth of 3.2% during the third
quarter of 2026, its biggest expansion in 12 quarters** , according to the
timely estimate of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) published this Friday by the
National Institute of Statistics and Geography (INEGI).

Compared with the immediately preceding quarter, GDP increased 0.9% in real
terms and with seasonally adjusted figures. With this result, the economy
accumulated two consecutive quarters of quarterly growth, although it
moderated its pace relative to the 1.5% advance registered in the second
quarter.

Growth was driven by tertiary activities, mainly related to services, which
**increased 1.1%** , and secondary activities, which include industry, with an
advance of 0.8%. In contrast, primary activities, corresponding to the
agricultural sector, decreased 0.4%.

## Services and Industry Drive Annual Growth

Compared with the same quarter of 2025, tertiary activities grew 3.3%;
secondary activities, 3.1%; and primary activities, 1.8%, according to the
timely estimate data.

The annual growth of 3.2% represented the Mexican economy's biggest advance in
12 quarters. In addition, GDP accumulated **four consecutive periods with
positive annual variations**.

![INEGI chart: annual real GDP growth, Q1 2023 to Q3
2026](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/inegi-gdp-
annual-q3-2026.png)Annual real GDP growth, Q1 2023–Q3 2026 (in Spanish).
Chart: INEGI, Timely Estimate of Quarterly GDP

During the first nine months of 2026, the economy registered annual growth of
1.9%, according to the preliminary results released following INEGI's
publication.

The institute specified that the data correspond to a timely estimate,
prepared with the statistical information available at the time of its
publication. The definitive figures will be released later and could show
modifications.

## Mexico's Performance and the U.S. Economy

The Mexican result coincides with an acceleration of the U.S. economy, the
main destination of the country's exports. Between January and September 2026,
the United States received **84.8% of Mexican non-oil exports** , according to
the data provided for this article.

The U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis reported that that country's GDP grew at
an annualized rate of 3.4% during the third quarter, compared with the 2.2%
advance registered in the previous period.

Mexican economic activity had faced pressures during 2025, amid the
uncertainty generated by U.S. President Donald Trump's trade policy and the
imposition of tariffs. Despite that environment, the country avoided an annual
contraction of its economy.

In early October, the International Monetary Fund projected growth of 1.5% for
Mexico in 2026, although it warned that external uncertainty continues to
represent a risk to its expansion.

The timely third-quarter figure offers a signal of greater dynamism, although
the definitive figures and the performance of the last period of the year will
make it possible to gauge the economic growth of 2026 more precisely.
